story.title: Andhra to Hackney
text: Frost & Flame is a delivery-only kitchen at 194 Hackney Road, London E2 7QL.
Stone ice cream is mixed to order on a frozen slab. Andhra pulao, chaats, curry bowls and drinks are made fresh for delivery across E1, E1W, E2, E8 and E9, or for collection from the kitchen.

play.note: A few light puzzles and a quiz you can play while you decide what to order.

puzzles.title: The mixed-up jars
puzzles.question: Three jars are labelled TEA, COFFEE and MIXED. Every label is wrong. You may draw one bean or leaf from one jar without looking inside. Which jar do you choose, and how do you relabel all three? Assume you can recognise tea from coffee.
hints: Start with the jar whose current label says MIXED.
Because that label is wrong, it must hold only one ingredient.
puzzles.answer: Draw from MIXED. If it is tea, that jar is TEA. The jar labelled COFFEE cannot be coffee (wrong label) or tea (already found), so it is MIXED. The jar labelled TEA is COFFEE. Reverse tea/coffee for a coffee draw.

puzzles.title: Four dessert orders
puzzles.question: Asha, Ben, Cara and Dev each chose one different dessert: cone, brownie, mango or jamun. Asha chose neither cone nor mango. Ben chose mango. Cara did not choose cone or jamun. Who chose what? Write a little grid before revealing.
hints: Cross out mango for everyone except Ben.
puzzles.answer: Ben: mango. Cara: brownie (not cone or jamun, and mango is taken). Asha: jamun (not cone/mango, brownie taken). Dev: cone. There is exactly one solution.

puzzles.title: The missing pound
puzzles.question: Three friends pay £30 for dinner. The correct bill is £25. A helper returns £1 to each friend and keeps £2. Each friend has paid £9: 3 × £9 = £27. Add the helper’s £2 and you get £29. Where is the missing pound?
hints: What is already included in the £27?
Separate money kept from money returned.
puzzles.answer: No pound is missing. £27 = £25 restaurant + £2 helper. Add the £3 returned, not the £2 again: £27 + £3 = £30.

puzzles.title: The nine-scoop balance
puzzles.question: Nine sealed scoop pots look identical. Eight weigh the same; one is heavier. You have a balance scale and only TWO weighings. How can you always identify the heavier pot?
hints: Split into three groups of three.
The first weighing identifies a group, not a single pot.
puzzles.answer: Weigh three against three. If balanced, the heavy pot is in the untouched three; otherwise it is in the heavier group. From those three weigh one against one. A heavier side wins; if balanced, the third is heavy.

questions.q: What does the Scoville scale describe?
questions.fact: The original Scoville test used dilution and human tasters.
Wilbur Scoville introduced his test in 1912.

questions.q: Which protein in dairy milk helps disperse capsaicin?
questions.fact: Casein can help make capsaicin easier to wash away.
Saffron is the dried stigma of Crocus sativus.

questions.q: Which spice is made from bark?
questions.fact: Cinnamon comes from the inner bark of Cinnamomum trees.

questions.q: Vanilla comes from which plant family?
questions.fact: Vanilla pods are fruits of orchids.

questions.q: Black, green and white peppercorns commonly come from what plant?
questions.fact: Processing and ripeness create different peppercorn products.
The unopened flower buds of Syzygium aromaticum become cloves.

questions.q: Tea leaves come from which plant?
questions.fact: Black and green teas can come from the same species, processed differently.
